audit.title: Create Automation-Compatible Contracts

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong lead — "A contract is Automation-compatible when it follows a specified interface that allows the Chainlink Automation Network to determine if, when, and how the contract should be automated." Sections mostly open with the answer; the "Example… custom logic" section opens with requirements rather than a one-line summary.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H2 hierarchy, 0 level skips, no oversized sections (max 560 words). The trigger-selection logic is a bullet list that would extract far better as a table. No tables present (measured: 0).

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Thin — only 4 prose numerals, 0 with units. Mentions `interval` of 60 and `v1.3.0` but no gas-limit ceilings, `checkUpkeep` execution constraints, or supported-network counts inline.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good density — 17 links, 3 to GitHub primary sources. Weakened by 3 opaque anchors ("here", "this") that don't tell an engine what's behind them.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The compatibility definition is crisp and liftable; interface names are consistently backticked. `checkUpkeep`/`performUpkeep` lack a one-line definition each near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no `TechArticle` schema. Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; the single `sol` block is complete with imports and pragma `^0.8.20`, labeled by language, and carries explicit "DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION" framing. No action needed. (The "identifiers never assigned" flag is comment prose, not real code gaps.)

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers setup and both major triggers plus Vyper, but no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased sections (e.g. "checkUpkeep returns true but performUpkeep never runs").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent entity naming ("Chainlink Automation Network", interface names). No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured Chainlink Automation guide with a strong canonical definition and one complete, runnable Solidity example. Its biggest GEO strength is code completeness — the snippet ships with SPDX, pragma, imports, and constructor. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates were served) plus a missing trigger→interface comparison table and symptom-phrased troubleshooting coverage. The verdict: solid content that under-signals to engines and misses retrieval on how-do-I / error-string queries.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema + canonical + dates
recommendations.issue: measured — "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, and a self-referential `canonical` URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-trust and E-E-A-T for agent ingestion.

recommendations.title: Add a trigger → interface comparison table
recommendations.where: "Automation compatible contracts" section, replacing/augmenting the bullet list
recommendations.issue: "The interface you use will depend on the type of trigger you want to use:"
recommendations.change: Add a 3-column table: Trigger type | Interface | When to use (log event → `ILogAutomation`; onchain custom logic → `AutomationCompatibleInterface`; time → time-based upkeep, no interface; Data Streams → `StreamsLookupCompatibleInterface`).
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract the decision and justify a recommendation; this is the page's core selection question.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.change: Add "Troubleshooting" with H3s phrased as queries: "checkUpkeep returns true but performUpkeep is never called", "Upkeep runs out of funds", "Vyper checkData array size error". Answer each in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: devs and agents query by symptom; concept-titled prose loses that retrieval even when it contains the answer.

recommendations.title: Replace opaque link anchors
recommendations.where: "You can learn more about these interfaces [here]", "architecture [here]", Vyper "[here]"
recommendations.change: Use descriptive anchors, e.g. "the Automation interfaces reference", "the KeepersConsumer Vyper example".
recommendations.why: descriptive anchor text tells engines what the target authorizes, raising citation quality.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics for Automation constraints
recommendations.where: "Custom logic Automation compatible contracts must meet the following requirements"
recommendations.issue: measured — "0 [numerals] with units"; no limits stated
recommendations.change: State inline the `checkUpkeep` gas limit, `performUpkeep` gas limit, and the current supported-network count with a link, plus that `checkUpkeep` is simulated offchain at block cadence.
recommendations.why: quantitative limits are among the highest-lift additions for generative visibility.

recommendations.title: Add one-line definitions for `checkUpkeep` / `performUpkeep`
recommendations.issue: functions described mid-sentence, not as liftable definitions
recommendations.change: Lead each bullet with a self-contained sentence: "`checkUpkeep` is the offchain-simulated view function that returns whether an upkeep should run."
recommendations.why: crisp verbatim definitions near first use are preferentially quoted.

antiPatterns: Opaque cross-reference anchors ("here", "this") ×3 — weakens link attribution.
No visible last-updated date — freshness cannot be signaled to engines.
No undifferentiated prose walls, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff. Code is properly tagged and complete.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; confirm it indexes this URL.
Site-level JSON-LD/schema defaults and canonical-URL emission are template concerns beyond this single page.
The served content lacked any `<head>` metadata; pass raw `<head>` through the CLI to confirm whether schema/canonical exist but were not captured.
